picks.excerpt: A new report says OpenAI and Jony Ive's io first hardware device will be a portable, screenless smart speaker with a camera and sensors that read the user's surroundings - pitched as an AI-first 'home computer' rather than a phone-style gadget.
picks.rationale: Biggest, most novel story in the pool - the first concrete shape of the OpenAI x Jony Ive device (screenless AI-first speaker) signals where post-phone AI hardware is headed.

picks.excerpt: Ahead of the July 22 Galaxy Unpacked, Samsung teased the Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 as an 'AI-powered health companion' promising real-time AI health insights, better tracking accuracy and new internal hardware.
picks.rationale: Timely pre-Unpacked hardware teaser positioning on-wrist AI health as the headline; the single best-sourced version of a story doubled by GSMArena.

picks.excerpt: Meta is adding rate limits to AI features on its Ray-Ban smart glasses, capping Conversation Focus at three hours a month free and gating 15 hours behind a $20/month Meta One Premium plan - an early sign of AI-glasses features moving to subscriptions.
picks.rationale: High-actionability trend signal - AI wearable features shifting behind subscriptions; distinct from the earlier super-sensing story and a real cost-of-AI shift for anyone building on the platform.

picks.excerpt: Samsung's health notice signals One UI 9 Watch arriving this month, adding an AI-driven Blood Pressure Trend feature to Galaxy Watches while retiring Vascular Load in the US - a shift in the watch's on-device health-sensing stack.
picks.rationale: Concrete software/feature change (AI Blood Pressure Trend, Vascular Load retirement) distinct from the hardware teaser; a fourth distinct outlet keeps the final set at 4 unique stories and 4 outlets.
